{"claims":[{"claim_text":"The Employee Free Choice Act (EFCA) would restore the original intent of the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB).",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The Employee Free Choice Act (EFCA) would permit workers to choose union representation without fear and intimidation.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"If a majority of workers demonstrated their choice to form a union, the Employee Free Choice Act (EFCA) would certify it without a delay-ridden and coercive election process.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Employer stonewalling on negotiating a first collective agreement could trigger an arbitration process under the Employee Free Choice Act (EFCA).",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Penalties for serious abuses of workers’ rights to organize would be stiffened under the Employee Free Choice Act (EFCA).",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Business and the right-wing are ferociously opposed to any restoration of the right to freely organize.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Only a major mobilization by outraged citizens demanding the right to freely organize could put enough spine in timid Democratic politicians to pass any substantive reform like the Employee Free Choice Act (EFCA).",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"The actual implementation of social and economic rights is always dependent on an aroused citizenry willing to organize and fight for them.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[3]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
